title: Adding noise step by step
objectives: Derive the closed form for a point after many noising steps, and compute it for a schedule.

screens.title: Blur the rings
screens.prose: Three hundred points on two rings, radii 0.8 and 1.6. At every step we shrink each point a little towards the origin and add a little fresh noise. Slide through the steps.
screens.question: Roughly when can you no longer see two separate rings?

options.why: At step 5 the rings are only slightly blurred; the gap between them is still clear.

options.text: Only at step 50, the last step
options.why: By step 30 the two rings have merged into one cloud.

options.text: Never: the rings stay visible throughout
options.why: Slide to step 30 or 50: one round cloud remains.

hints.text: Look for the empty gap between the rings.

feedback.correct: Right. By step 20 the gap has filled in; by step 50 there is one round cloud.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Slide through the steps and watch the gap between the rings.

explain.text: The gap closes between steps 10 and 20. At step 50 the cloud is round and centred, close to pure noise: only $\sqrt{0.0045} \approx 0.067$ of each point is left.

screens.title: One noising step
screens.prose: This is the **forward process** of a diffusion model: $$\mathbf{x}_t = \sqrt{1 - \beta_t}\,\mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \sqrt{\beta_t}\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t,$$ with fresh standard normal noise $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t$ each step. Take $\mathbf{x}_{t-1} = (1.6, 0)$, $\beta_t = 0.2$ and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t = (0.5, -1)$.
screens.question: Fill in $\mathbf{x}_t$, to 3 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Shrink by $\sqrt{0.8}$, then add $\sqrt{0.2}$ times the noise.

byKey.noshrink: You added the noise without shrinking the point first.

explain.text: The point shrinks to $(1.431, 0)$ and the noise adds $(0.224, -0.447)$, giving $(1.655, -0.447)$.

screens.title: The product that matters
screens.prose: Write $\alpha_t = 1 - \beta_t$ and $\bar\alpha_t = \alpha_1\alpha_2\cdots\alpha_t$, the running product. A toy schedule has $\beta = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$ for steps 1 to 3.
screens.question: What is $\bar\alpha_3$? Give a decimal.

explain.text: $\bar\alpha_3 = 0.9 \times 0.8 \times 0.7 = 0.504$. It says how much of the starting signal's variance survives three steps.

screens.title: Two steps in one
screens.prose: Show that two steps give $\mathbf{x}_2 = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_2}\,\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar\alpha_2}\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ for one standard normal $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$.
screens.question: Put the steps in order. Leave out the step that does not belong.

lines.text: The bracket is a sum of independent normals with mean 0, so it is normal with variance $\alpha_2(1 - \alpha_1) + (1 - \alpha_2) = 1 - \alpha_1\alpha_2$ (`random-vars` l10).
So the bracket equals $\sqrt{1 - \bar\alpha_2}\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ in distribution, and $\sqrt{\alpha_1\alpha_2} = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_2}$.
The bracket has standard deviation $\sqrt{\alpha_2(1 - \alpha_1)} + \sqrt{1 - \alpha_2}$, the sum of the two.
lines.why: Standard deviations of independent normals do not add; variances do.

byKey.x: You added standard deviations. For independent noise, variances add.

explain.text: The two noise terms are independent, so their variances add to $1 - \bar\alpha_2$. By induction any step $t$ is $\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar\alpha_t}\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$: sample it in one go.

screens.title: The original schedule
screens.prose: Ho, Jain and Abbeel (2020) used 1,000 steps with $\beta_t$ rising linearly from $10^{-4}$ to 0.02. That gives $\bar\alpha_{500} \approx 0.0786$ and $\bar\alpha_{1000} \approx 4.0 \times 10^{-5}$.
screens.question: At step 500, what is the coefficient of $\mathbf{x}_0$, $\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{500}}$? Give a decimal to 2 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. The signal's coefficient is the square root of $\bar\alpha_t$.

byKey.abar: That is $\bar\alpha_{500}$ itself; take its square root.

explain.text: Halfway through, 0.28 of the signal is left; at step 1,000 it is $\sqrt{4.0 \times 10^{-5}} \approx 0.0064$, effectively pure noise.

screens.title: This level's schedule
screens.prose: Our models use $T = 50$ steps with $\beta_t$ rising linearly from $10^{-3}$ to 0.2. The curves show $\bar\alpha_t$, the signal's share of the variance, and $1 - \bar\alpha_t$, the noise's. At the end $\bar\alpha_{50} \approx 0.0045$.
screens.question: What is the standard deviation of the signal part of $\mathbf{x}_{50}$, for a unit-variance coordinate of $\mathbf{x}_0$? Give a decimal to 3 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Scale the unit sd by $\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{50}}$.

byKey.abar: That is $\bar\alpha_{50}$, a share of variance. Take its square root for an sd.
byKey.noise: That is the noise part's sd.

explain.text: Only 0.067 of the signal's sd survives, against 0.998 for the noise: the last step is nearly pure noise, as the hook showed.

screens.title: Why shrink first
screens.prose: By the closed form, $\operatorname{Var}(x_t) = \bar\alpha_t\operatorname{Var}(x_0) + (1 - \bar\alpha_t)$ for each coordinate. Our rings have $\operatorname{Var}(x_0) \approx 0.8$ per coordinate, and at step 20, $\bar\alpha_{20} \approx 0.4432$.
screens.question: What is the variance of a coordinate at step 20? Give a decimal to 2 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the shrunk signal variance and the noise variance.

byKey.signal: That is the signal part alone; add $1 - \bar\alpha_{20}$ for the noise.
byKey.one: The variance is exactly 1 only for unit-variance data. Ours is 0.8.

explain.text: The variance moves from 0.8 towards 1 and never overshoots: 0.91 at step 20. For data scaled to variance 1 it stays at 1 throughout, which is why each step shrinks by $\sqrt{1 - \beta_t}$.

screens.title: Noise without shrinking
screens.prose: A colleague writes the step as $\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \sqrt{\beta_t}\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t$, leaving out the shrink. With our 50 betas, which add up to 5.025, and data of variance 0.8 per coordinate:
screens.question: What is the variance of a coordinate after 50 such steps? Give a decimal to 3 places.

hints.text: Without shrinking, each step adds $\beta_t$ to the variance.

feedback.correct: $0.8 + 5.025 = 5.825$, and it keeps growing with more steps.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Each step adds its $\beta_t$; nothing is taken away.

byKey.one: 1 is what the shrinking version approaches. Without the shrink the variance only grows.
byKey.sum: You left out the data's own variance, 0.8.

explain.text: Without the shrink the variance climbs to 5.825, so the end is not a standard normal and the scale depends on $T$. The $\sqrt{1 - \beta_t}$ factor keeps the total at about 1.

screens.title: An end that is not noise
screens.prose: Another schedule keeps $\beta_t = 0.01$ for all 50 steps.
screens.question: What is $\bar\alpha_{50}$ for it? Give a decimal to 3 places.

feedback.correct: $0.99^{50} \approx 0.605$: most of the signal is still there.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Raise $1 - 0.01$ to the 50th power.

explain.text: About 0.605 of the signal's variance remains, so $\mathbf{x}_{50}$ is far from pure noise. Sampling then starts from a standard normal that is the wrong distribution; l16 shows what that costs.

screens.title: A familiar step
screens.prose: One noising step, $x_t = \sqrt{1 - \beta}\,x_{t-1} + \sqrt{\beta}\,\epsilon_t$ with a fixed $\beta$, is a time-series model you have met (`arma` l2).
screens.question: Which one?

options.text: A random walk, which has no pull back towards 0
options.why: A random walk has coefficient 1. Here it is below 1, so the series is pulled back towards 0.

options.text: An MA(1), a moving average of the last two noise terms
options.why: The step feeds back the last value of $x$, not the last noise term.

options.text: A trend with drift, rising a fixed amount each step
options.why: There is no drift term; the mean shrinks towards 0.

hints.text: Is the last value fed back?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Look at how $x_{t-1}$ enters.

explain.text: It is an AR(1) with $\phi = \sqrt{1 - \beta}$ and noise variance $\beta$, whose stationary variance is exactly 1. Diffusion runs such a process until the data are forgotten.

ideas: The forward step shrinks by $\sqrt{1 - \beta_t}$ and adds $\sqrt{\beta_t}$ times fresh noise; with $\bar\alpha_t = \prod_{s \le t}(1 - \beta_s)$ it has the closed form $\mathbf{x}_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,\mathbf{x}_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar\alpha_t}\,\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$.
The closed form follows because variances of independent normals add. Our 50-step schedule ends at $\bar\alpha_{50} \approx 0.0045$, nearly pure noise.
The shrink keeps unit-variance data at variance 1; without it the variance grows with every step.
summary.trap: Adding noise without shrinking, so the variance grows with $t$; or adding standard deviations instead of variances.
